result.title: Check out my technological uplifting, civilization-building, and science in a magic world fiction!

contents.markdown:
Why? It's a "How to (re)build civilization" book embedded in a Roman-inspired progression fantasy setting.

This is my premise in a short comic format:

[![r/rational - Check out my technological uplifting, civilization-building, and science in a magic world fiction!](https://preview.redd.it/check-out-my-technological-uplifting-civilization-building-v0-w7pbjsj7da2h1.png?width=1254&format=png&auto=webp&s=5a0900e3c4c5412c4fc20578edc0dbc55d10798f)](https://preview.redd.it/check-out-my-technological-uplifting-civilization-building-v0-w7pbjsj7da2h1.png?width=1254&format=png&auto=webp&s=5a0900e3c4c5412c4fc20578edc0dbc55d10798f "Image from r/rational - Check out my technological uplifting, civilization-building, and science in a magic world fiction!")

My main focus beyond technology is the social side of innovation and progress. How ancient natural philosophy is fundamentally limiting as a framework by mixing aesthetics into physics and such issues.

Because technological development isn't just about inventing things or even teaching science, it's about making society accept and adapt to the changes. And surviving the enmity of the people whose feet you step on, both physically and politically.

Link to my story and its blurb: [https://www.royalroad.com/fiction/163319/noble-scholar-mage-a-practical-guide-to-industrializing](https://www.royalroad.com/fiction/163319/noble-scholar-mage-a-practical-guide-to-industrializing)

  

PS: I hope it's ok to post something like this here, I found a few comments saying it's fine, but not offical policy. I'll remove it if it's not permitted.
